questions.q: What does a `/query` response's `done` field being `false` indicate?
options: The query failed and returned no records
The query syntax was invalid
The response does not yet contain every matching record, and nextRecordsUrl should be called to continue
The org has run out of API requests for the day
questions.explain: done: false means more matching records exist beyond this batch; nextRecordsUrl tells you where to fetch the next batch from.

questions.q: What are the three fields present in every /query response body?
options: status, message, errorCode
totalSize, done, records
id, success, errors
page, limit, offset
questions.explain: totalSize gives the total match count, done indicates completeness, and records holds the actual matching records in this batch.

questions.q: What is the main difference between SOQL (via /query) and SOSL (via /search)?
options: SOQL filters one specific object with field-based conditions; SOSL searches text across multiple object types in one call
SOSL can only be used for Delete operations
SOQL and SOSL are two names for the exact same thing
SOSL cannot return more than one record
questions.explain: SOQL is scoped to a single object with precise WHERE conditions, while SOSL performs a text search that can span several object types at once.

questions.q: Which resource is the REST equivalent of SOAP's queryMore call for paging through a large query result?
options: /limits
/search
/sobjects/describe
The nextRecordsUrl returned in a /query response when done is false
questions.explain: Following nextRecordsUrl to fetch the next batch of results serves the same purpose in REST that queryMore served in SOAP.

questions.q: Which scenario is the better fit for SOSL rather than SOQL, according to this lesson?
options: A global search box where a user types a term and you don't know in advance which object type(s) might match
Filtering Accounts where Industry equals a specific known value
Retrieving a single record by its known ID
Updating a record's phone number
questions.explain: A global, text-based search across unknown object types is the classic SOSL use case, since SOQL always targets one specific object.
